TR-R6-2: the comment cites retention.js L35 for the ordering and spec 'Retention and deletion' L773 for what it says. TR-R6-4: the 7 d + 1 min test stamps the file with the pinned upload time and asserts imageFilesLeft 0, orphans 0, no new image.orphan_delete event and no file of the image left; the one-line no-unlink mutant survives the old test (ev:ev-mv4ak5zf-01832ede) and is killed by the new one (ev:ev-mv49opld-0190c44d), at real-clock shifts +0/14/30/400 days (ev:ev-mv4ajsjq-01e0ae52: the old test survives at +0 and +14 and is killed only from +30). DATE ROBUSTNESS. Audit of src: Date.now/new Date outside the injected clock are in src/clock.js (the system clock itself), src/config.js loadConfig (RS_DEMO_DATE default: tests set it), the three AI providers (default clock, main.js injects its own), src/db/connection.js (busy deadline, a duration), performance/hrtime (durations), http/static.js (ETag from mtime, no behaviour); cookies use Max-Age (relative, so Chromium's real clock cannot expire a pinned-clock session); sessions, CSRF, rate limits, OAuth token cache, webhook time window, leases, reservations all use the injected clock; there is no TLS in the application or tests (the webhook certificate is never fetched). The ONE place where file-system time meets the injected clock is retention.js orphan age (clock.now() - mtimeMs): correct in production (same clock), but under a pinned clock a file the test just wrote carries the real date. Fix: a comment in retention.js stating this, a test (exactly 1 day removed, 1 ms younger kept, a file stamped after the pinned clock kept; killed by the |age| mutant, ev:ev-mv49xotr-01551c66) and explicit utimes stamping in the 7 d + 1 min test. METHOD: scratchpad/rework7-tools/shift-clock.mjs is a preload (NODE_OPTIONS --import, inherited by every spawned Node child) that moves Date.now()/new Date() and all file times (stat family +shift, utimes -shift) by CLOCK_SHIFT_DAYS, like a system clock that moved. Final tree plus the foreign-file patch, full locked npm test at +0, +14 and +30 days: 2341 tests, 2333 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped each (ev:ev-mv4a8wvv-0178c772, ev:ev-mv4ab3q6-0166b77a, ev:ev-mv4ade0v-01ca2bd5); browser suite with the Node side at +30 days: 14/14 (ev:ev-mv4aea7f-01c08c76). No other test or product code depends on the real date; nothing needs to change in test/helpers/**. An earlier +14 probe (ev:ev-mv49rblt-01dcc7be) is not valid: the preload variable was then named RS_SHIFT_DAYS, which server-proc.js blanks for child servers (RS_ prefix), so the children ran on the unshifted clock; renamed CLOCK_SHIFT_DAYS.
